$comment: Every fixed prose formulation of the md projection, keyed by the construct that owns it. A {placeholder} is filled by the renderer with that construct's data; a placeholder the renderer does not fill (e.g. `{slot}`) stays literal. Imported by the compiler and bundled into the apx engine: one set of words for every projection.

CHECK.$comment: A checked condition head (src/check.ts): IF!/UNTIL! (level 1, the agent sees the condition, the judge decides), IF!!/UNTIL!! (level 2, sealed). {head} = If / Until, {run} = the apx's check command. `question` and `state` are what the judge is asked, built by the compiler and the apx.

IF.1: {head} {condition} — run `{run}`: its answer decides, not your own judgement

UNTIL.1: {head} {condition} — after each round run `{run}` and repeat until it answers open, at most {rounds} rounds: its answer decides, not your own judgement; at the limit, stop and report that the gate stayed closed
UNTIL.2: Repeat until `{run}` answers open — run it after each round, at most {rounds} rounds; at the limit, stop and report that the gate stayed closed

CHECK.nextRound: round {round} of {rounds} — do the next round, then {again}
CHECK.limit: round limit reached ({round} of {rounds}): stop and report that {end}
CHECK.question: In the state, {condition}?

WHEN.head: When
WHEN.$comment: `handed`: WHEN handed <contract>: — the trigger's input is an instance of that contract (its spec, shaped as the contract's AS template), read from the apx.
WHEN.handed: Its input is an instance of the contract `{name}`{ref} — its spec, shaped as that contract's template, as the apx hands it to you.

EACH.$comment: An EACH block (D56): `{list}` the list variable's read, `{item}` the element's read `{{item}}`, `{max}` its bound; `{waited}` when a line in it is not started in the background.
EACH.head: For each element of {list}, at most {max} runs — a list longer than {max} is an error: stop the flow and report it. In each run `{item}` is its element. Every line below runs once per element, all the runs at once{waited}; an INTO collects one result per run — a list, in element order; a run that fails does not stop the others: its result goes on with theirs
EACH.waited: — wait for every run of a line not started in the background before you go on

RUN.flow: Run the flow `{name}`{ref} — start with `{command}`: it says how
RUN.name: `{name}`

DELEGATE.$comment: A DELEGATE line (src/delegation.ts): the form says the context — all of it, or only what its AS template holds; `~` starts it in the background.
DELEGATE.background: — start it in the background and go on: its WAIT takes it back
DELEGATE.started: — first `{apx} delegate start {id}`; it ends with `{apx} delegate deliver {id} -` (its result on stdin) or `{apx} delegate block {id} "<why>"`: say so when you hand it over
DELEGATE.elements: (one id per run: <k> is the run's number, from 1)
DELEGATE.contracts: Hand every contract `{list}` holds to `{agent}`, one each, all at once{background}
DELEGATE.contractsRun: — `{apx} contract start {mark} --by {agent}` opens a copy for each and names it; hand each one to `{agent}` with its id: it reads its spec with `{apx} contract get <ctr-id>`, works in its copy and ends with `{apx} delegate deliver <ctr-id>` or `{apx} delegate block <ctr-id> "<why>"`
DELEGATE.contractsWait: ; then `{apx} wait {mark}`: every delivery is merged and lands in the working folder
DELEGATE.contractsHarness: Hand every contract `{list}` holds to `{agent}` on {harness}, another harness, one each, all at once{background}
DELEGATE.contractsHarnessRun: — `{apx} contract start {mark} --by {harness}:{agent}` opens a copy for each, writes its prompt — its spec and its zones — and prints the command that launches `{agent}` on {harness} in it, on the model its BUDGET tier maps to there, with the rules to run it by; run every command with your shell, then for each contract `{apx} delegate deliver <ctr-id> --answer` (its answer, and what its copy changed within its zones) or `{apx} delegate block <ctr-id> "<why>"`
DELEGATE.harnessContext: , handing over the task and the variables it reads
DELEGATE.harnessBackground: — in the background: run its command in the background and go on; its WAIT takes it back
DELEGATE.harnessRun: — first `{apx} delegate start {id}`: it opens the piece's own copy of the project and prints the command that launches `{agent}` on {harness}, with the rules to run it by; run that command with your shell, then `{apx} delegate deliver {id} --answer` (its answer, and what it changed in its copy within its perimeter) or `{apx} delegate block {id} "<why>"`
DELEGATE.harnessWait: ; then `{apx} wait {id}`: what it changed is merged and lands in the working folder

ASK.$comment: An ASK line — an agent's question to a delegate (`BY`, else the default delegate): its contract hands over its input; the answer takes its INTO variable's template.

FORK.$comment: A FORK line: the work runs on the conversation itself — a copy of whoever runs it, or `BY y` that agent on it.
FORK.self: {text} — a fork of yourself, with this whole conversation{shaped}{background}
FORK.agent: {text} — to `{agent}`, forked with this whole conversation{shaped}{background}
FORK.shaped: ; what you hand it is shaped as `{name}`{ref}

MARK.$comment: A MARK line (D16–18): zones of the code bound to contracts, each a promise that waits until a DELEGATE starts it.
MARK.text: {criterion} — read the code and choose the zones: for each one write its spec as `{spec}`{ref} and run `{apx} contract mark {mark} -` (the spec on stdin); it gives the contract its id — write `agent-pack <ctr-id>` where the zone starts and `agent-pack end <ctr-id>` where it ends, each inside a comment; a file with no comments is not marked. At most {max} zones{within}. They make up `{list}`; nothing starts yet
MARK.within: ; each contract may also write within the domain `{domain}`
MARK.none: No zone fits: mark none, and the DELEGATE of `{list}` has nothing to start

WAIT.$comment: A WAIT line: it waits for every piece it names, then the variables hold each one's state — delivered or blocked (allSettled).
WAIT.named: {names} — every one delivered or blocked; then go on with each one's result
WAIT.all: everything this step started in the background — every piece delivered or blocked; then go on with each one's result
WAIT.run: — `{apx} wait {ids}{max}`: it returns when each one is delivered, blocked or ended without delivery, or when the limit is reached; for any not delivered you decide — wait again, `{apx} delegate take <dlg-id>`, `{apx} delegate reassign <dlg-id> <agent>` or `{apx} delegate block <dlg-id> "<why>"`

COMPUTE.require: The program refuses the input — it stops with an error — unless:

procedure.1: A delegate carries out this procedure — never carry it out yourself{how}.
procedure.2: A program carries out this procedure — never carry it out yourself{how}.

EXECUTOR.ask: — hand it over its input and the shape of its answer, both from `{apx} delegate input {id}`, then store its answer: `{apx} delegate answer {id} -`

answer.shaped: # answer AS `{name}` — JSON only, shaped like:

EXECUTOR.rounds: ; after each round, ask again — at most {rounds} rounds: at the limit, stop and report that the condition never held

into.1: — hand it over its input and the shape of its answer, both from `{apx} delegate input {id}`, then store its answer as `{name}`: `{apx} delegate answer {id} - --into {name}`

APPLIES.$comment: Where a policy, a skill or a dimension holds (src/withUse.ts): its perimeter, or only under a WITH that names it — a dimension has no perimeter; `ls` is the apx listing's short form.

scope.team: Applies to the members of team `{name}`.
scope.with: Applies only to the work nested under a line that names it.

WRITES.$comment: An agent's perimeter: the domains `@WITHIN` puts it within — {globs} are their WRITES globs; READS the globs it only reads. With no READS among them it reads whatever it needs.
fence: > Do NOT modify or create files outside these patterns without explicit user authorisation — they belong to others.
WRITES.none: > This agent writes no file — do NOT modify or create any without explicit user authorisation.
WRITES.formula: the files a judge placed in “{formula}” (`apx scope` lists them)
WRITES.uncertain: > A judge could not tell whether these files belong — decide each in context, from what the work needs: {files}.

READS.only: > Read only: {globs} — and what you may write.

LENS-IN.line: You must read every request through the template **{name}**{ref} — it is the shape your input arrives in.

LENS-OUT.bridge: You must answer every such request by filling **{name}**{ref}.

VAR.readShaped: {read}, keeping only what fits {template} and shaped as it
VAR.block: Work out `{name}` — its value is the outcome of the lines below:
VAR.store: When done, store the result as `{name}`: `{command}`, the value on stdin.
VAR.storeTyped: When done, store the result as `{name}`: `{command}`, the value on stdin as JSON with the fields of that template.
VAR.entry: Read it: `{read}` — store it: `{write}`, the value on stdin.

intro: You are an agent-pack agent. What follows is your definition, compiled from `.ap` source — treat its directives, policies, and orchestration as authoritative.
Every reference to another block carries its id: read that block before acting on it, never guess its content.

quiz.ask: A reference to another block appears in your definition. What do you do before acting on it?
options: guess its content from its name
skip it if the task looks clear
read that block, by its id

quiz.ask: How do you read your definition?
options: the part the task needs, when it needs it
all of it, every time
only the first chapter

intro: WHEN      interpreting the policies listed in this chapter
MUST      apply every policy in this chapter, cumulatively, wherever its scope line says it applies
!MUST     weigh a policy against convenience or speed

quiz.ask: When may you set a policy aside?
options: when it slows the task down
never where its scope line says it applies — every such policy applies, all together
when the user seems in a hurry

intro: WHEN      interpreting the role profiles listed in this chapter
MUST      treat them as a layered cognitive identity that applies together
!MUST  treat them as exclusive alternatives

quiz.ask: A role shapes how you think and act. When does it apply?
options: only when the task is about it
always — every role listed, together with your own rules
pick the one that fits the task

template.scaffold: Produce **{name}** by filling this layout — replace every `{slot}`, keep the rest verbatim:
intro: WHEN      a `shape your response as \`<slug>\`` marker appears anywhere in this prompt, followed by the template's reference
MUST!     produce your answer in that shape — the template its reference points to
MUST      fill the shape's layout, replacing every `{slot}` with concrete content, keeping all literal text verbatim
MUST      respect each field's type, constraints, and rules — constraints are guidance you self-enforce
MUST      when a field references another template (`**<slug>**` and its reference), fill one instance of that template per item
SHOULD    imitate the <example> block when present — it shows the exact target format
!MUST  deviate from the shape's structure, add fields, or reorder the layout

quiz.ask: You are told to shape your response as a template. What do you produce?
options: its layout filled exactly — every slot replaced, literal text verbatim
free text inspired by it
its layout plus any field you find useful

intro: WHEN   you encounter a `Run the procedure <name>` line in a flow
MUST   follow the steps of the procedure its reference points to

quiz.ask: You meet `Run the procedure <name>`. What do you do?
options: improvise steps that reach the same goal
follow that procedure's steps as written
skip it when the task seems done

intro: MUST      run the flow's steps in the order they appear, and carry out each step's lines yourself — you run the flow

MUST      on a `Delegate` line, hand its task to the agent or team it names, matched to that name's purpose, with the context its form says: all your context, or only what its template holds — shape what you hand over as that template, at the stated severity; a team takes it as one agent: run the flow its routing picks, and take that flow's result as the line's answer
MUST      on a `Fork` line, hand its task to a fork of yourself, or to the agent it names, on this whole conversation

MUST      start in the background, and go on, what a line says to start in the background — issue those delegate calls in parallel; on a `Wait for` line, wait until every piece it names is delivered or blocked, then go on with each one's result
!MUST     re-enter a flow already running earlier in the chain

quiz.ask: How do you run a flow?
options: steps in any order, all by yourself
steps in order, carrying out each step's lines yourself
only the steps you judge useful

skill.$comment: A skill the agent IMPORTs: an agent-pack skill (its own apx, {command}) or one of the harness (`@harness.skills`, {name}). An adapter may say `apx` / `harness` in its own words: renderings.SKILL.
intro: MUST      use a skill of this chapter wherever its scope line says it applies
MUST      load a skill the way its entry says before you follow it

quiz.ask: A skill is listed in your definition. When do you use it?
options: whenever you judge it fits the task
where its scope line says it applies — loaded the way its entry says
never — skills are for other agents

skill.apx: Load it when you need it: run `{command}` and follow what it prints.
skill.harness: Load it when you need it: it is a skill of your harness — `{name}`.

store.home: Its records live in `{file}`, from the project root — read and write them only with the commands below, never the file. {lasts}

lasts.project: It survives between sessions — what you write stays.
lasts.session: It lasts for this session only.

store.usage: Use it — these are the exact commands, with this store's own fields:
store.unknownType: **This store cannot be used.** `{name}` declares `DRIVER {declared}`, which is not an installed driver — available: {available}.
intro: MUST      keep what must outlive the conversation in the stores listed in this chapter
MUST      read and write a store only through the commands given with it
!MUST     touch a store's files directly

quiz.ask: Where do you keep what must survive between sessions?
options: in any file you choose
in your answer
in a store, through its commands only

dimension.$comment: A dimension (D43): an answer about the code the apx keeps, by file. {read} and {write} are the apx commands of its operations.
dimension.covers: Files: {globs} — each: {each} — its value: a list of records with the fields of the store `{name}`{ref}, or `none` when there is nothing to report.
dimension.read: Read it: `{read} <file>` — `hit` gives the answer, `miss` says why there is none.
dimension.write: On a `miss`, once you have worked the answer out, write it — JSON on stdin, or `none`: `{write} <file> [refs=<path>;<path>] - < value.json`
dimension.query: Search the answers by their fields: `{q} <field>=<value> …` — fresh answers only; to fill it, `{next}` hands you the next file it has no fresh answer for.
intro: Answers about the code, already worked out and kept by the apx. Each dimension says what it holds and which files it covers; the lines it is for are the ones nested under a line that names it.
MUST      on a `hit`, use its answer — once read, whether you also need the code is your call
MUST      on a `miss`, once you have worked the answer out, write it with the dimension's write command, shaped as its template
!MUST     touch the cache under `.agent-pack/cache/` directly

quiz.ask: The lines you are on are nested under a line that names a dimension. What do you do?
options: work the answer out from the code
read the dimension: on a hit, use its answer — and read the code too only if you still need it
open its cache file

plugin.$comment: A plugin's block (src/plugins.ts): its lines as written, then the commands its apx serves it with — each the plugin's own operation on the block's id.

domain.$comment: A domain (D44): a region of the code — the files work within it writes, those it only reads. `@WITHIN <domain>` puts work within one; the perimeter fence lists their globs.
domain.formula: the {count} files a judge placed in “{formula}”
intro: The regions of the code. The scope warning at the top of this definition says the files of the domains you work within — what you write, and what you only read.
!MUST     write a file outside the domains you write — say what you would change, and why, instead

quiz.ask: To finish your work you need to change a file of a domain you only read. What do you do?
options: change it, the work needs it
leave it, and say what you would change and why
copy it into a domain you write

team.heading: # Your team
team.member: You are `{agent}`, a member of the team `{team}` (purpose: {purpose}).
team.closing: Requests are routed to the team by an orchestrator; stay within your responsibility, don't bypass routing.

unit.members: Your members — each answers through its own command:

intro: WHEN      a user request needs to be routed to one or more agents
MUST      pick the agent or team whose purpose matches the task
MUST      when targeting a team, apply its routing to pick a member
MUST      delegate to the chosen agent and treat its output as the response
MUST      issue parallel delegate calls when tasks are independent

MUST      when a member lists an input shape (`talk to it as \`<slug>\``), shape what you hand it as that template — it is the member's default; a flow step that declares its own shape contract overrides it
!MUST  delegate to a team-member directly, bypassing its routing

quiz.ask: A request targets a team. Who handles it?
options: the member the team's routing picks
any member you like
every member at once

main.heading: # {name}{about}
main.boot: Your rules, teams and flows live in the main. Run it at the start of your work and follow what it prints:
main.again: If what it printed is no longer in your context, run it again.

unit.teams: Your teams — each one's routing and flows are its own:
unit.members: Your agents — each answers through its own command:

tool.heading: Tool named "{name}"
intro: WHEN   a tool's body describes a capability relevant to the current task
MUST   use the tool by following the instructions in its body

quiz.ask: When do you use a listed tool?
options: always, on every task
when the task needs what its body describes, following its instructions
never without asking

decorators.$comment: A block decorator (src/decorators.ts): the opening of its sentence is its own; each block it names reads so, joined.

intros.WITHIN: For the work below, act only within

apx.$comment: What the apx says on its verbs. `deliver`: a contract delivered from its copy (`delegate deliver <ctr-id>`) — `refused` the reason it is not, `done` what it says when it is.

refused.notRunning: {id} is {state} — only a running contract is delivered
refused.lostZones: {id} was not delivered — the marks of its zones are lost in {files}: put them back around your work, as they were written
refused.strayed: {id}: nothing changed in its copy, and {files} changed in the project folder — the work goes in its copy: {copy}
refused.leftOut: {id} was not delivered — what is left out stays out only with a good reason: {cmd} delegate deliver {id} --why "<reason>"; or undo it in the copy
